# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary:
Returns all cells in one board column as an ordered list from top to bottom.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the column index.
2. Iterate over all rows from 0 to numRows - 1.
3. Collect the cell at (row, col) for each row.
4. Return the resulting list.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- A list of Cells in the given column, ordered by increasing row index.
Pre-condition:
- col is within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified row and column indices from the board.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that row and col are within board bounds.
2. Access the cell from the internal 2D board structure.
3. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- The Cell located at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- The requested coordinates must be within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified Position on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Delegate to the board storage to retrieve the cell.
4. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The Cell located at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to a valid in-bounds board location.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary:
Counts and returns the number of Gem entities currently present on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Iterate over all board cells.
2. For each EntityCell, inspect its entity.
3. Count entities that are instances of Gem.
4. Return the total count.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input:
- None.
Output:
- The number of Gems still present on the board.
Pre-condition:
- The board structure is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary:
Returns the EntityCell located at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Access the cell at that position and cast/interpret it as an EntityCell.
4. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The EntityCell at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to an in-bounds board location containing an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary:
Returns all cells in one board row as an ordered list from left to right.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row index.
2. Iterate over all columns from 0 to numCols - 1.
3. Collect the cell at (row, col) for each column.
4. Return the resulting list.

- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary:
Returns the EntityCell at the specified row and column indices.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row and column indices.
2. Access the cell at (row, col) from the internal board structure.
3. Interpret the cell as an EntityCell and return it.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows

Related Classes: EntityCell, GameBoard

- col: zero-based column index.

Output:
- The EntityCell located at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- The requested location is within bounds and corresponds to an EntityCell.

- The board is not modified.

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary:
Returns all cells in one board column as an ordered list from top to bottom.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the column index.
2. Iterate over all rows from 0 to numRows - 1.
3. Collect the cell at (row, col) for each row.
4. Return the resulting list.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- A list of Cells in the given column, ordered by increasing row index.
Pre-condition:
- col is within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified row and column indices from the board.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that row and col are within board bounds.
2. Access the cell from the internal 2D board structure.
3. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- The Cell located at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- The requested coordinates must be within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified Position on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Delegate to the board storage to retrieve the cell.
4. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The Cell located at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to a valid in-bounds board location.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary:
Counts and returns the number of Gem entities currently present on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Iterate over all board cells.
2. For each EntityCell, inspect its entity.
3. Count entities that are instances of Gem.
4. Return the total count.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input:
- None.
Output:
- The number of Gems still present on the board.
Pre-condition:
- The board structure is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary:
Returns the EntityCell located at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Access the cell at that position and cast/interpret it as an EntityCell.
4. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The EntityCell at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to an in-bounds board location containing an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary:
Returns all cells in one board row as an ordered list from left to right.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row index.
2. Iterate over all columns from 0 to numCols - 1.
3. Collect the cell at (row, col) for each column.
4. Return the resulting list.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- Valid range: 0 <= row < numRows.
Output:
- A list of Cells in the given row, ordered by increasing column index.
Pre-condition:
- row is within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary:
Returns the EntityCell at the specified row and column indices.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row and column indices.
2. Access the cell at (row, col) from the internal board structure.
3. Interpret the cell as an EntityCell and return it.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, GameBoard
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- The EntityCell located at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- The requested location is within bounds and corresponds to an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary:
Returns all cells in one board column as an ordered list from top to bottom.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the column index.
2. Iterate over all rows from 0 to numRows - 1.
3. Collect the cell at (row, col) for each row.
4. Return the resulting list.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- A list of Cells in the given column, ordered by increasing row index.
Pre-condition:
- col is within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified row and column indices from the board.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that row and col are within board bounds.
2. Access the cell from the internal 2D board structure.
3. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
- Valid range: 0 <= row < numRows and 0 <= col < numCols.
Output:
- The Cell located at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- The requested coordinates must be within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary:
Returns the cell at the specified Position on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Delegate to the board storage to retrieve the cell.
4. Return the cell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: Cell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The Cell located at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to a valid in-bounds board location.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary:
Returns the number of Gem entities currently present on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Traverse the board and inspect each cell.
2. For each EntityCell, check whether its entity is a Gem.
3. Count all Gem entities found.
4. Return the total count.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Gem, EntityCell, Cell
Input:
- None.
Output:
- The number of Gems still present on the board.
Pre-condition:
- The board structure is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.
- The returned value equals the number of Gems remaining on the GameBoard.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary:
Returns the EntityCell located at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the input Position.
2. Validate that the position is within board bounds.
3. Access the cell at that position and cast/interpret it as an EntityCell.
4. Return the EntityCell.
Related Features:
- GameBoard.board
- GameBoard.numRows
- GameBoard.numCols
Related Classes: EntityCell, GameBoard, Position
Input:
- position: board coordinates as a Position.
- Valid range: position.row and position.col must be within the board bounds.
Output:
- The EntityCell at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null and refers to an in-bounds board location containing an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board is not modified.

GameBoard::getRow

Returns all cells in one board row as an ordered list from left to right.

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary:
Reverses the effects of a previously executed Alive move by restoring the board state from the supplied move result.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the given MoveResult.
2. If it is not an Alive result, do nothing.
3. Move the player back to the original position stored in the prior move record.
4. Restore any collected Gems and ExtraLives to their original positions.
5. Reverse any finite life increase caused by collected ExtraLife items as needed by game state logic.
Related Features:
- GameBoardController.gameBoard
- GameBoard.player
- MoveResult hierarchy
- Alive.collectedGems
- Alive.collectedExtraLives
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveResult, Alive, Position, Gem, ExtraLife, Player
Input:
- prevMove: the previous move result, expected to be an Alive result.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- prevMove is either null or a previously returned MoveResult from makeMove.
- If prevMove is Alive, its recorded positions are valid board positions.
Post-condition:
- If prevMove is Alive, the board and player state are restored to the state before that move.
- If prevMove is not Alive, no state change is required.

GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary:
Executes one player move in the given direction using inertial sliding rules and returns the corresponding move result.
Algorithm:
1. Determine the player's current Position and the direction delta.
2. Repeatedly advance one step at a time using Position offset operations.
3. Stop when one of the following occurs:
   - the next step is outside the board: stop before leaving the board;
   - the next cell is a Wall: stop before the Wall;
   - the next cell is a StopCell: move onto that cell and stop;
   - the next cell contains a Mine: the move is Dead and movement stops immediately;
   - the next cell is blocked on the first step, yielding zero distance: return Invalid.
4. While moving through cells on an Alive path, record and remove any Gem or ExtraLife encountered.
5. If a Mine is encountered, do not remove any passed Gems/ExtraLives and restore the board/player state to the original position.
6. If the final stop is normal (boundary, Wall, or StopCell) and at least one step was moved, return an Alive result with the new position and collected item positions.
7. If the first step is blocked, return Invalid.
Related Features:
- GameBoardController.gameBoard
- GameBoard.player
- GameBoard.getCell1 / getCell2
- GameBoard.getEntityCell1 / getEntityCell2
- Position.offsetByOrNull1 / offsetByOrNull2
- MoveResult hierarchy: Alive, Dead, Invalid, Valid
Related Classes: GameBoard, Position, PositionOffset, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Valid, Cell, EntityCell, Wall, StopCell, Gem, Mine, ExtraLife, Player
Input:
- direction: one of UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT.
Output:
- Alive: if the player slides at least one cell and stops normally without hitting a Mine.
- Dead: if the movement enters a Mine.
- Invalid: if the player cannot move at all on the first step.
- The returned MoveResult contains the newPosition for the final position of the player, or the original position for Dead as required.
Pre-condition:
- gameBoard and its player are initialized.
- The board contains a valid player position.
- direction is non-null.
Post-condition:
- For Alive: the player position is updated to the stopping cell/boundary-adjacent cell; collected Gems and ExtraLives are removed from the board and recorded in the result.
- For Dead: the player position is logically unchanged in the result, the board state is restored, and no passed Gem/ExtraLife is collected.
- For Invalid: neither the board nor player position changes.

The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoardController::undoMove
Summary:
Reverses the effects of a previously executed Alive move by restoring the board state from the supplied move result.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the given MoveResult.
2. If it is not an Alive result, do nothing.
3. Move the player back to the original position stored in the prior move record.
4. Restore any collected Gems and ExtraLives to their original positions.
5. Reverse any finite life increase caused by collected ExtraLife items as needed by game state logic.
Related Features:
- GameBoardController.gameBoard
- GameBoard.player
- MoveResult hierarchy
- Alive.collectedGems
- Alive.collectedExtraLives
Related Classes: GameBoard, MoveResult, Alive, Position, Gem, ExtraLife, Player
Input:
- prevMove: the previous move result, expected to be an Alive result.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- prevMove is either null or a previously returned MoveResult from makeMove.
- If prevMove is Alive, its recorded positions are valid board positions.
Post-condition:
- If prevMove is Alive, the board and player state are restored to the state before that move.
- If prevMove is not Alive, no state change is required.

GameBoardController::makeMove
Summary:
Executes one player move in the given direction using inertial sliding rules and returns the corresponding move result.
Algorithm:
1. Determine the player's current Position and the direction delta.
2. Repeatedly advance one step at a time using Position offset operations.
3. Stop when one of the following occurs:
   - the next step is outside the board: stop before leaving the board;
   - the next cell is a Wall: stop before the Wall;
   - the next cell is a StopCell: move onto that cell and stop;
   - the next cell contains a Mine: the move is Dead and movement stops immediately;
   - the next cell is blocked on the first step, yielding zero distance: return Invalid.
4. While moving through cells on an Alive path, record and remove any Gem or ExtraLife encountered.
5. If a Mine is encountered, do not remove any passed Gems/ExtraLives and restore the board/player state to the original position.
6. If the final stop is normal (boundary, Wall, or StopCell) and at least one step was moved, return an Alive result with the new position and collected item positions.
7. If the first step is blocked, return Invalid.
Related Features:
- GameBoardController.gameBoard
- GameBoard.player
- GameBoard.getCell1 / getCell2
- GameBoard.getEntityCell1 / getEntityCell2
- Position.offsetByOrNull1 / offsetByOrNull2
- MoveResult hierarchy: Alive, Dead, Invalid, Valid
Related Classes: GameBoard, Position, PositionOffset, Direction, MoveResult, Alive, Dead, Invalid, Valid, Cell, EntityCell, Wall, StopCell, Gem, Mine, ExtraLife, Player
Input:
- direction: one of UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT.
Output:
- Alive: if the player slides at least one cell and stops normally without hitting a Mine.
- Dead: if the movement enters a Mine.
- Invalid: if the player cannot move at all on the first step.
- The returned MoveResult contains the newPosition for the final position of the player, or the original position for Dead as required.
Pre-condition:
- gameBoard and its player are initialized.
- The board contains a valid player position.
- direction is non-null.
Post-condition:
- For Alive: the player position is updated to the stopping cell/boundary-adjacent cell; collected Gems and ExtraLives are removed from the board and recorded in the result.
- For Dead: the player position is logically unchanged in the result, the board state is restored, and no passed Gem/ExtraLife is collected.
- For Invalid: neither the board nor player position changes.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Position::offsetBy1
Summary: Returns a new Position translated by the given row and column deltas.
Algorithm:
1. Compute newRow = row + dRow.
2. Compute newCol = col + dCol.
3. Create and return a new Position(newRow, newCol).
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position
Input:
- dRow: signed row delta.
- dCol: signed column delta.
Output:
- Returns a new Position offset by the requested deltas.
Pre-condition:
- The current Position is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The original Position is unchanged.
- The result represents the translated coordinate.

Position::offsetBy2
Summary: Returns a new Position translated by the provided PositionOffset.
Algorithm:
1. Read dRow and dCol from the PositionOffset.
2. Delegate to offsetBy1(dRow, dCol).
3. Return the new Position.
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input:
- offset: a PositionOffset containing signed dRow and dCol.
Output:
- Returns a new Position offset by offset.dRow and offset.dCol.
Pre-condition:
- offset is non-null.
Post-condition:
- The original Position is unchanged.

Position::offsetByOrNull1
Summary: Returns the translated Position if it remains inside the board, otherwise returns null.
Algorithm:
1. Compute the candidate position using row + dRow and col + dCol.
2. Check whether candidate.row is within [0, numRows - 1].
3. Check whether candidate.col is within [0, numCols - 1].
4. Return the candidate if both checks pass; otherwise return null.
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input:
- dRow: signed row delta.
- dCol: signed column delta.
- numRows: total number of board rows, positive.
- numCols: total number of board columns, positive.
Output:
- Returns the translated Position if it is within bounds; otherwise null.
Pre-condition:
- numRows > 0 and numCols > 0.
- The current Position is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The original Position is unchanged.

Position::offsetByOrNull2
Summary: Returns the translated Position if it remains inside the board, otherwise returns null.
Algorithm:
1. Read dRow and dCol from the PositionOffset.
2. Delegate to offsetByOrNull1(dRow, dCol, numRows, numCols).
3. Return the result.
Related Features: row, col
Related Classes: Position, PositionOffset
Input:
- offset: a PositionOffset containing signed dRow and dCol.
- numRows: total number of board rows, positive.
- numCols: total number of board columns, positive.
Output:
- Returns a new Position if the offset stays within bounds; otherwise null.
Pre-condition:
- offset is non-null.
- numRows > 0 and numCols > 0.
Post-condition:
- The original Position is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

- The returned value is the previous entity reference.
- The StopCell contains only a Player entity after the operation.

2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
MoveStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the most recently pushed MoveResult from the stack and records that an undo has occurred.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that the stack is not empty.
2. Remove the top MoveResult from the moves list.
3. Increment popCount by one.
4. Return the removed MoveResult.
Related Features: moves, popCount
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the removed top MoveResult.
Pre-condition:
- The stack is not empty.
Post-condition:
- The returned MoveResult is no longer stored in the stack.
- popCount increases by one.

MoveStack::peek
Summary: Returns the top MoveResult without removing it from the stack.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that the stack is not empty.
2. Return the last pushed MoveResult without removing it.
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the top MoveResult.
Pre-condition:
- The stack is not empty.
Post-condition:
- The stack contents are unchanged.

MoveStack::push
Summary: Pushes a new MoveResult onto the stack for later undo.
Algorithm:
1. Append the provided move to the end of the moves list.
2. Leave popCount unchanged.
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input:
- move: the MoveResult to store; normally an Alive result.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- move is non-null.
Post-condition:
- move becomes the top of the stack.
- popCount is unchanged.

MoveStack::isEmpty
Summary: Checks whether the stack contains no stored MoveResult entries.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the moves list.
2. Return true if it contains no elements; otherwise false.
Related Features: moves
Related Classes: MoveStack, MoveResult
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns true if the stack is empty.
Pre-condition:
- The stack is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The stack contents are unchanged.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit.

Entity::setowner
Summary: Sets or updates the owner EntityCell of this Entity and returns the previously associated owner.
Algorithm:
1. Save the current owner reference in a local variable oldOwner.
2. Assign the input owner to this.owner.
3. Return oldOwner.
Related Features: owner
Related Classes: EntityCell, Entity
Input:
- owner: the EntityCell that will own this Entity; may be null only if the implementation allows detaching an entity from a cell.
Output:
- Returns the previous EntityCell owner reference, or null if none existed.
Pre-condition:
- The provided owner must be a valid EntityCell instance if non-null.
- The call must not violate the bidirectional association invariants between Entity and EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- this.owner refers to the provided owner.
- The returned value is the previous owner reference.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

- None.
Output:
- Returns the updated death count.

- The game state is initialized.
Post-condition:
- numDeaths increases by exactly one.

GameState::getGameBoardView
Summary: Creates and returns a view object bound to this game board.
Algorithm:
1. Create a new GameBoardView using the current gameBoard.
2. Return the created view.
Related Features: gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoardView, GameBoard
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns a GameBoardView associated with the current GameBoard.
Pre-condition:
- gameBoard is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The game state is unchanged.
- The returned view references the current board.

GameState::getScore
Summary: Computes and returns the current score according to the game scoring formula.
Algorithm:
1. Compute collectedGems = initialNumOfGems - getNumGems().
2. Compute score = initialBoardSize + (collectedGems * 10) - numMoves - (moveStack.popCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4).
3. Return score.
Related Features: initialNumOfGems, numDeaths, numLives, numMoves, gameBoard, moveStack
Related Classes: GameState, GameBoard, MoveStack
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the current integer score.
Pre-condition:
- initialNumOfGems and gameBoard are initialized.
- The board size used in scoring is defined as the total number of cells in the initial board configuration.
Post-condition:
- The game state is unchanged.
- The returned value reflects the scoring formula:
  Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - Moves - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4).

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

GameState::getScore
Summary: Computes and returns the current score according to the game scoring formula.
Algorithm:
1. Obtain the remaining gem count from getNumGems().
2. Compute collectedGems = initialNumOfGems - remainingGems.
3. Compute score = InitialBoardSize + (collectedGems * 10) - numMoves - (moveStack.popCount * 2) - (numDeaths * 4).
4. Return score.
Related Features: initialNumOfGems, numDeaths, numMoves, moveStack, gameBoard
Related Classes: GameState, MoveStack
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the current integer score.

- The board size used in scoring is the total number of cells on the initial board.
Post-condition:
- The game state is unchanged.
- The returned value reflects the scoring formula:
  Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - Moves - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4).

GameState::increaseNumLives
Summary: Increases the number of lives by the specified amount and returns the new life count.
Algorithm:
1. If the game uses unlimited lives, leave numLives unchanged and return Integer.MAX_VALUE.
2. Otherwise, add delta to numLives.
3. Return the updated numLives.
Related Features: numLives, UNLIMITED_LIVES

Pre-condition:
- delta >= 0.
Post-condition:
- Finite lives are increased by delta.
- Unlimited lives remain unlimited.

Summary: Increases the number of lives by the specified amount and returns the new life count.
Algorithm:
1. If the game uses unlimited lives, leave numLives unchanged and return Integer.MAX_VALUE.
2. Otherwise, add delta to numLives.
3. Return the updated numLives.
Related Features: numLives, UNLIMITED_LIVES
Related Classes: GameState
Input:
- delta: non-negative integer amount to add to the current finite lives.
Output:
- Returns the updated number of lives, or Integer.MAX_VALUE in unlimited-lives mode.
Pre-condition:
- delta >= 0.
Post-condition:
- Finite lives are increased by delta.
- Unlimited lives remain unlimited.

Algorithm:
1. If the game is in unlimited lives mode, return Integer.MAX_VALUE.

Related Features: numLives, UNLIMITED_LIVES

- None.

- The game state is initialized.
Post-condition:

4. Return the updated numLives.
Related Features: numLives, UNLIMITED_LIVES

- delta >= 0.
Post-condition:
- Finite lives are reduced by delta, not below zero.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns all Cells from the specified column as a list ordered from top row to bottom row.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the column index.
2. Iterate over all rows from 0 to numRows - 1.
3. Collect board[row][col] into a list.
4. Return the list.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- col: zero-based column index.
Output:
- Returns a list of Cells in the given column, ordered by increasing row.
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned list contains exactly numRows Cells.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Returns the Cell located at the specified row and column indices.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that row and col are within board bounds.
2. Access board[row][col].
3. Return the referenced Cell.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
Output:
- Returns the Cell at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= row < numRows.
- 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned Cell belongs to the board at the requested position.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Returns the Cell at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the given Position.
2. Delegate to getCell1(row, col).
3. Return the result.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell, Position
Input:
- position: a board coordinate containing row and col.
Output:
- Returns the Cell located at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null.
- position.row and position.col are within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Counts and returns the number of Gem entities currently present on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Initialize count to 0.
2. Scan every cell on the board.
3. Increment count for each cell containing a Gem.
4. Return count.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Gem, EntityCell
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the number of Gems remaining on the board as a non-negative integer.
Pre-condition:
- The board structure is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned value reflects the current number of Gem entities on the board.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Returns the EntityCell at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the given Position.
2. Delegate to getEntityCell2(row, col).
3. Return the result.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, EntityCell, Position
Input:
- position: a board coordinate containing row and col.
Output:
- Returns the EntityCell at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null.
- The position must refer to a cell that is an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns all Cells from the specified row as a list ordered from left column to right column.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row index.
2. Iterate over all columns from 0 to numCols - 1.
3. Collect board[row][col] into a list.
4. Return the list.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
Output:
- Returns a list of Cells in the given row, ordered by increasing column.

- 0 <= row < numRows.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned list contains exactly numCols Cells.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2

2. Access board[row][col].
3. Cast or interpret the cell as an EntityCell.
4. Return it.

- col: zero-based column index.

- Returns the EntityCell at (row, col).

- The board state is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
GameBoard::getCol
Summary: Returns all Cells from the specified column as a list ordered from top row to bottom row.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the column index.
2. Iterate over all rows from 0 to numRows - 1.
3. Collect board[row][col] into a list.
4. Return the list.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- col: zero-based column index.
Output:
- Returns a list of Cells in the given column, ordered by increasing row.
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned list contains exactly numRows Cells.

GameBoard::getCell1
Summary: Returns the Cell located at the specified row and column indices.
Algorithm:
1. Validate that row and col are within board bounds.
2. Access board[row][col].
3. Return the referenced Cell.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
Output:
- Returns the Cell at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= row < numRows.
- 0 <= col < numCols.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned Cell belongs to the board at the requested position.

GameBoard::getCell2
Summary: Returns the Cell at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the given Position.
2. Delegate to getCell1(row, col).
3. Return the result.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell, Position
Input:
- position: a board coordinate containing row and col.
Output:
- Returns the Cell located at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null.
- position.row and position.col are within board bounds.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.

GameBoard::getNumGems
Summary: Counts and returns the number of Gem entities currently present on the board.
Algorithm:
1. Initialize count to 0.
2. Scan every cell on the board.
3. Increment count for each cell containing a Gem.
4. Return count.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Gem, EntityCell
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Returns the number of Gems remaining on the board as a non-negative integer.
Pre-condition:
- The board structure is initialized.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned value reflects the current number of Gem entities on the board.

GameBoard::getEntityCell1
Summary: Returns the EntityCell at the specified Position.
Algorithm:
1. Read row and col from the given Position.
2. Delegate to getEntityCell2(row, col).
3. Return the result.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, EntityCell, Position
Input:
- position: a board coordinate containing row and col.
Output:
- Returns the EntityCell at the given Position.
Pre-condition:
- position is non-null.
- The position must refer to a cell that is an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.

GameBoard::getRow
Summary: Returns all Cells from the specified row as a list ordered from left column to right column.
Algorithm:
1. Validate the row index.
2. Iterate over all columns from 0 to numCols - 1.
3. Collect board[row][col] into a list.
4. Return the list.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, Cell
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
Output:
- Returns a list of Cells in the given row, ordered by increasing column.
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= row < numRows.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.
- The returned list contains exactly numCols Cells.

GameBoard::getEntityCell2
Summary: Returns the EntityCell located at the given row and column.
Algorithm:
1. Validate row and col bounds.
2. Access board[row][col].
3. Cast or interpret the cell as an EntityCell.
4. Return it.
Related Features: board, numRows, numCols
Related Classes: GameBoard, EntityCell, Cell
Input:
- row: zero-based row index.
- col: zero-based column index.
Output:
- Returns the EntityCell at (row, col).
Pre-condition:
- 0 <= row < numRows.
- 0 <= col < numCols.
- board[row][col] is an EntityCell.
Post-condition:
- The board state is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
1.Overview
This project implements a grid-based puzzle game called Inertia. The core mechanic is inertial sliding: once the player chooses a direction, the character slides continuously in that direction until it hits a Wall or enters a StopCell. The objective is to navigate the board to collect all Gems while avoiding Mines that cause death and life loss. The game features a scoring system, life management, and an Undo system to backtrack moves.
2.Functional Requirements
The system manages 2D grid coordinates and their deltas through the Position and PositionOffset classes for all
movement calculations and boundary checks. In GameBoardController.makeMove, when a move is initiated via a Direction,
the player piece moves step-by-step from its current Position. If the player successfully slides at least one cell and the movement ends by a normal stopping condition, such as a Wall, boundary, or StopCell, without hitting a Mine, the result is Alive. During an Alive move, any Gem or ExtraLife passed through is collected, removed from the board, and recorded in the Alive result.
 Sliding stops immediately before a Wall, at the board boundary, or exactly
on a StopCell. StopCell is a special cell type that can only contain a Player entity. Hitting a Mine causes a Dead result and stops movement. The position recorded for the player after a Dead move is the original position. The board remains unchanged from before the move, and any Gem or ExtraLife passed before the Mine is not collected or removed.
A move returns
Invalid when the player cannot move at all (blocked by Wall or boundary on the first step, resulting in zero movement
distance). Every move must return a MoveResult (Alive, Dead, or Invalid); collected Gems and ExtraLives are recorded only in Alive results.
 In GameState, getNumGems() returns the number of Gems still present on the GameBoard (i.e., remaining Gems).A player wins when there are no Gems left on the board (getNumGems() == 0). A player loses when lives reach zero (unless in unlimited lives mode).For scoring, the number of collected Gems is initialNumOfGems - getNumGems(), and the score is calculated as : Score = InitialBoardSize + (CollectedGems * 10) - (Moves * 1) - (Undoes * 2) - (Deaths * 4). If numLives is less than zero, the player has unlimited lives, and
getNumLives returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. 
In GameController.processMove, Invalid moves do not change counters and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Alive moves increment numMoves, apply collected ExtraLife effects, and are pushed to the MoveStack. Dead moves increment numMoves and numDeaths, decrease finite lives by one, and are not pushed to the MoveStack. Only Alive moves are undoable.
processUndo pops one Alive move if available, restores the player position and collected Gems/ExtraLives, reverses finite ExtraLife gains, and returns true. If no move is available, it returns false. Undo does not decrement numMoves; undo count is represented by MoveStack.popCount.

GameStateSerializer: A tool for loading/saving the game state from/to text format, handling the mapping between characters (W, P, S, G, M, L) and Ecore classes. 
InertiaTextGame: The main runner handling the STDIN loop and parsing user commands like U, D, Undo, or Quit. 
```
